claims: At pinned PS2Recomp commit c5a9d02573410a2085a4b4b831b0b68ba3515440, the 13 listed packed-register templates and runtime macros extract under the recorded file hashes.
The source-pinned synthetic probe checks 80096 cases for each of the 13 listed operations and reports zero mismatches under UBSan.

The check covers only the extracted host vector templates, tested aliases and the modeled zero-register macros; it does not establish instruction flags, timing, decoder behavior, full emulator behavior, or game equivalence.

The earlier audit's compile failure was an unused PCPYH wrapper parameter under -Werror, and its second run's mismatches came from a wrong test-oracle source-buffer selection; the corrected harness changed that test setup and passed.

evidence.text: Pinned PS2Recomp commit c5a9d02573410a2085a4b4b831b0b68ba3515440. Header ps2xRuntime/include/ps2_runtime_macros.h SHA-256 c0dfe8104803a380ff4f38a3ba3d5ed1979c68ad7234d83230863f079f354c4e. Helper ps2xRecomp/src/lib/mmi_translation_helpers.cpp SHA-256 1402bdb9f81923a8c91c7fa790399a2563ebc5f7cd0c899b7c29cb7c6bafc5ee. sse2neon.h SHA-256 78632498a57bf7e080e84cb8d74c47ce93b204cece77eab79de2908eb8bc92ed.

The final source-pinned verifier compiled actual generated templates with Clang -std=c++20 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -fsanitize=undefined and the pinned SSE2NEON header. It reported names [PCPYLD, PCPYUD, PCPYH, PEXTLW, PEXTUW, PEXTLH, PEXTLB, PAND, POR, PNOR, PXOR, PSUBB, PSUBW], checks 80096 for each, mismatches 0 for each, run exit 0, empty stderr.

Probe inputs are synthetic vectors: four basis cases, eight deterministic boundary/pattern cases, and 10,000 seeded random pairs. Eight register modes include distinct registers, rd==rs, rd==rt, rd==0 with sentinel, rs==0, rt==0, both sources zero, and rd==rs==rt. This verifies only these extracted template expressions in this host probe; it does not exercise game routines, instruction decode, flags, timing, or complete emulation.

The first scratch harness compile failed only because PCPYH's generated wrapper did not mark unused RS as used while -Werror was enabled. The second scratch harness executed but mismatched because expected-input setup selected the wrong source vector in a register mode. The final harness corrected the test-only input-buffer selection; no upstream source was changed.
